question: Can activation subspaces that are jointly active and output-relevant be isolated as compact, causally necessary-and-sufficient algorithmic cores, and do their coordinates or fitted dynamics expose mechanisms invariant across training seeds, checkpoints, architectures, and scale?

key_findings.claim: Algorithmic Core Extraction (ACE) combines activation covariance with task-output sensitivity, then treats the resulting leading subspace as a candidate causal realization of the task.
key_findings.evidence: For centered activations H and stacked output Jacobians J, ACE takes the SVD of their interaction HJ^T, maps leading left modes back through H^T, and QR-orthogonalizes them into a projector P. A candidate core is called sufficient when Ph preserves the task metric and necessary when h-Ph reduces it to approximately chance; a linear operator can then be fitted in core coordinates and interpreted spectrally.

key_findings.claim: In the controlled Markov experiment, a three-dimensional core is both behaviorally sufficient and necessary under the paper's ablation criterion.
key_findings.evidence: Three one-layer 64-dimensional transformers reach test accuracy 0.748 on a four-state chain whose chance and Bayes-optimal accuracies are 0.25 and 0.75. Core-only accuracy remains 0.748 for all three models, while core-removed accuracy is 0.261, 0.237, and 0.247. The extraction uses a 99.9% energy threshold over all test activations without ablation refinement.

anchors.section: Table A1 and B, Markov Chain Experiment

key_findings.claim: The Markov cores occupy different geometric subspaces but encode nearly identical state information and transition spectra.
key_findings.evidence: Pairwise projector overlap is 0.027-0.031 and principal angles are 76-89 degrees, whereas two canonical correlations per pair are 0.999 and the third is 0.927-0.958. Least-squares core operators reproduce the nontrivial chain eigenvalues 0.75+/-0.25i and approximately 0.50 (0.51, 0.49, 0.48).

anchors.section: Table A2 and B, operator fitting

key_findings.claim: Near-unity CCA in the Markov setting does not by itself identify a unique shared mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: Each three-dimensional core is a near-sufficient encoding of the same four discrete states, so invertible state representations are expected to be highly canonically correlated even when their embeddings are unrelated. The paper does not compare ACE with PCA, supervised state encoders, random sufficient subspaces, or another active-subspace method on this experiment.

anchors.section: A, note on ACE reducing to PCA

key_findings.claim: On modular addition, ACE detects a causal core and rotational operator at the same checkpoint at which the three models grok.
key_findings.evidence: Three two-layer transformers trained on addition modulo 53 remain near chance and then reach perfect test accuracy around epoch 800. At grokking, ablation-defined cores form and eigenvalues of fitted add-one operators move to the unit circle, recovering cyclic dynamics without prespecifying a Fourier mode.

anchors.section: C, operator fitting and held-out transitions

key_findings.claim: Continued weight decay makes the modular-addition core less compact, not more compact.
key_findings.evidence: After branching the models at epoch 900, retaining weight decay 1 grows the extracted core from roughly 15 toward 60 dimensions and fills nearly all 26 nonzero Fourier-frequency bins; setting weight decay to zero keeps the core and mode count comparatively stable. The number of sufficient dimensions stays stable while the number whose removal destroys performance grows.

anchors.section: C, post-grokking branch and mode count

key_findings.claim: The paper's 'invariant core' is an equivalence-class claim, not evidence that independent models converge to the same physical subspace or even the same Fourier realization.
key_findings.evidence: Markov projectors are nearly orthogonal; modular-addition runs select different rotational modes and multiplicities; and modular cores change dimension under continued training. What recurs is task information, causal effect, or coarse operator structure up to coordinates, while the actual subspaces and modal implementations diverge.

key_findings.claim: A minimum-norm argument explains why weight decay can distribute a modular-addition solution across every available Fourier mode, but it depends on strong structural assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation assumes nonnegative mode amplitudes, approximately orthogonal parameter subspaces, an additive margin with fixed contrasts, negligible post-memorization task gradient, and a corrective force proportional to weight decay. Under those assumptions the minimum-norm coefficient vector is parallel to the contrast vector and uses all modes; these premises are not derived from the trained transformer or AdamW dynamics.

key_findings.claim: The predicted grokking delay fits the reported sweeps, but changing the modulus does not isolate functional redundancy.
key_findings.evidence: Across 12 seeds per condition, the weight-decay sweep gives an exponent about -1.02 and the seven-prime modulus sweep is fit by -Omega log(1-p_crit/p) with R^2 greater than 0.99, Omega about 2,770, and p_crit about 23. Yet p simultaneously changes vocabulary size, dataset size p^2, the target function, and the number of Fourier modes; the modulus sweep also uses full-batch training whereas the weight-decay sweep uses minibatches. No control varies redundancy while holding the task fixed.

key_findings.claim: ACE extracts a one-dimensional late-layer subject-verb-number axis in each of six pretrained language models.
key_findings.evidence: The models span GPT-2 Small/Medium/Large, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, and Qwen2.5-32B. Each selected layer has core rank one and a spectral gap from 40 to 531 except GPT-2 Large, whose reported gap is 2.8e10; selected layers range from 11/12 to 42/42 and 62/64.

key_findings.claim: The one-dimensional axis has a large causal effect on the paper's controlled agreement score.
key_findings.evidence: Across the six models, baseline AUC is 0.808-0.934, core-only AUC is 0.918-0.997, core-removed AUC is 0.102-0.244, and reflecting the activation across the axis yields AUC 0.021-0.092. The evaluation uses 1,200 constructed prompts and a margin defined only from is/are/was/were logits.

key_findings.claim: Cross-model coordinate correlations demonstrate shared label ordering, but not a unique shared subspace across architectures.
key_findings.evidence: On the same prompt set, signed one-dimensional coordinates have within-GPT-2 Spearman correlations 0.878-0.923 and cross-family correlations 0.585-0.934, with Pearson correlations 0.616-0.943 across families. Different models have different dimensional spaces, so no projector can be aligned directly; any strong singular/plural feature can correlate through the common ground-truth label and prompt difficulty. Uniqueness against alternative causal number axes is not tested.

key_findings.claim: The open-ended steering experiment is targeted by the same four-verb score and is reported qualitatively rather than as a general generation benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: At every decoding step, a clean pass gates intervention using probability mass on is/are/was/were; a second probing perturbation estimates local gain; and a third pass applies the strength needed to cross the same singular-plural margin. Figure 6 shows two selected continuations and no corpus-level rate of agreement errors, non-verb transfer, fluency loss, or collateral semantic change, so it does not establish that one axis governs agreement throughout unrestricted generation.

key_findings.claim: Core-only sufficiency is metric- and distribution-specific, not sufficiency for the model's complete behavior.
key_findings.evidence: All LLM necessity/sufficiency claims refer to a four-token agreement AUC on templated prompts after an intervention at one selected layer. Projecting away almost the entire residual state is off-distribution and can improve that narrow AUC, but language-model loss, grammaticality outside the templates, and other simultaneous computations are not evaluated under core-only ablation.

key_findings.claim: ACE's claimed blind automation still relies on task-specific choices and lacks method baselines.
key_findings.evidence: The analyst chooses a layer, task-output map, energy threshold, and optional causal rank refinement; modular-addition dynamics are then fitted to answer centroids under a hand-defined add-one transition. Appendix A concedes that ACE can reduce to PCA when activity and relevance align. No PCA, PLS, CCA, DAS, random-subspace, or computational-cost comparison is reported.

anchors.section: A, rank selection and PCA note
C-D, operator fitting and layer sweep

key_findings.claim: The paper explicitly leaves complex multi-step reasoning, systematic task decomposition, and nonlinear core dynamics untested.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion notes that low-dimensionality for multi-step reasoning is unknown, extracting task-specific cores requires a precise question, and possible nonlinear reductions or Koopman operators remain future work. The three demonstrations cover one stochastic synthetic process, modular addition, and one binary linguistic dependency.

method.core_idea: Treat mechanisms as equivalence classes of causally effective activation subspaces and fitted dynamics rather than individual neurons, heads, or weight coordinates. Extract directions that jointly carry activation energy and output sensitivity, validate them by complementary ablations, and inspect low-dimensional operators for task structure.
method.mechanism: At a chosen layer, center activations H and stack Jacobians J of a task-specific output map. SVD the activation-sensitivity interaction, map its leading modes into activation space, and form a projector P. Test Ph and h-Ph for sufficiency and necessity, refine rank if needed, and fit operators in Q^T h coordinates. Across runs, compare causal metrics, CCA, coordinate correlations, and spectra; across training, track core rank and operator eigenvalues.
assumptions: A linear activation subspace at a single layer is an adequate unit of mechanism for the target behavior.
Task-specific output Jacobians and the selected activation distribution capture all relevant directions.
Large behavioral effects under core-only and core-removed ablation reflect the normal computation rather than off-manifold intervention artifacts.
CCA or correlated one-dimensional coordinates distinguish a shared algorithm from multiple label-equivalent encodings.
A linear least-squares operator on core coordinates is a faithful dynamical description rather than a predictive summary of grouped states.
The grokking theory's Fourier modes occupy approximately orthogonal parameter subspaces and contribute additively to a fixed classification margin.
Changing the modulus primarily changes the number of equivalent modes rather than task difficulty, vocabulary, or data geometry.

techniques.role: Extract directions that are both highly active and locally relevant to a chosen output map.
Operationalize subspace sufficiency and necessity by complementary activation interventions.
Fit linear dynamics in core coordinates and compare their eigenvalue spectra with task structure.
Compare the information carried by geometrically different cores across random seeds.
Reflect late-layer activations across the agreement axis and calibrate per-token intervention strength.
Test predicted scaling with weight decay and modular redundancy across multiple seeds.

evaluations.setting: Three independently initialized one-layer transformers on a four-state Markov chain
evaluations.metric: Next-token accuracy under full, core-only, and core-removed activations
evaluations.result: All full and three-dimensional core-only models score 0.748; core removal gives 0.261, 0.237, and 0.247.

evaluations.setting: Pairwise comparison of the three Markov cores
evaluations.metric: Projector overlap, principal angles, CCA, and fitted transition eigenvalues
evaluations.result: Overlap is 0.027-0.031 and angles 76-89 degrees, while CCA is 0.927-0.999 and fitted eigenvalues reproduce 0.75+/-0.25i and 0.48-0.51.
evaluations.baseline: The exact Markov transition spectrum and cross-seed geometric identity

evaluations.setting: Three two-layer transformers trained on addition modulo 53 for 20,000 epochs
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy, causal core rank, and add-one operator spectrum
evaluations.result: All grok around epoch 800 as compact causal cores and unit-circle rotational modes appear; continued weight decay later inflates cores from about 15 toward 60 dimensions and populates nearly all 26 nonzero modes.
evaluations.baseline: Pre-grokking checkpoints and branches with post-epoch-900 weight decay disabled

evaluations.setting: Modular-addition sweeps with 12 seeds per condition
evaluations.metric: Delay from 99% train accuracy to 99% test accuracy
evaluations.result: The weight-decay exponent is about -1.02; the modulus curve fits -Omega log(1-p_crit/p) with R^2 above 0.99, Omega about 2,770, and p_crit about 23.
evaluations.baseline: Predicted inverse scaling in weight decay and large-p redundancy

evaluations.setting: 1,200 controlled subject-verb prompts across six pretrained LLMs from 117M to 32B parameters
evaluations.metric: Agreement AUC under baseline, core-only, core-removed, and core-flipped activations
evaluations.result: Baseline is 0.808-0.934, core-only 0.918-0.997, core-removed 0.102-0.244, and core-flipped 0.021-0.092.
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified hidden states and chance AUC 0.5

evaluations.setting: The same prompts projected onto each model's signed agreement axis
evaluations.result: Within-GPT-2 correlations reach Spearman 0.878-0.923 and Pearson 0.924-0.968; cross-family ranges are 0.585-0.934 and 0.616-0.943.
evaluations.baseline: Within-family agreement as a ceiling and zero cross-model correlation

evaluations.setting: Adaptive agreement-axis reflection during autoregressive generation in all six models
evaluations.result: The intervention produces selected agreement violations and broader continuation changes, but only two examples are displayed and no aggregate success, selectivity, fluency, or semantic-preservation metric is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Unsteered continuations for the same prompts

limitations: Author-stated: core dimensionality and linear dynamics are untested for multi-step reasoning or other complex tasks.
Author-stated: extracting a task-specific core requires a precise mechanistic question, and systematic task decomposition remains open.
Author-stated: nonlinear dimensionality reduction, learned relevance maps, and Koopman-style operators are proposed rather than evaluated.
Reviewer inference: no method baseline establishes that the activation-Jacobian SVD is better or more selective than PCA, PLS, CCA, DAS, supervised probes, or random subspaces.
Reviewer inference: the Markov result has only four states and the modular-addition main result only three seeds, limiting the force of a universality claim.
Reviewer inference: the LLM study covers one binary linguistic dependency on templated prompts and measures only four verb logits.
Reviewer inference: cross-model scalar correlation can arise from common labels and prompt difficulty and does not identify a unique shared mechanism.
Reviewer inference: open-ended steering has no quantitative evaluation beyond selected examples and is adaptively gated by the same target verbs.
Reviewer inference: the inverse grokking law confounds redundancy with modulus, vocabulary, task, and dataset size.
Reviewer inference: no code execution, independent replication, confidence intervals for the three-model experiments, or computational-cost comparison is supplied in the paper.
failure_modes: A high-variance task feature can make ACE collapse to PCA, returning a descriptive rather than uniquely mechanistic subspace.
Core-only or core-removed projections can move activations off manifold and create behavior not used by the unperturbed network.
Multiple causal subspaces can encode the same label or activate dormant pathways, so necessity and steering do not guarantee identifiability.
Continued regularization can inflate a previously compact core, undermining low-dimensional interpretability at late checkpoints.
When task dynamics are nonlinear or history-dependent, a fitted linear operator can miss the actual algorithm despite good local prediction.
A one-dimensional grammar intervention can change token probabilities, fluency, and downstream semantics together, obscuring selectivity.
The grokking scaling law can fail when modes overlap, capacity is insufficient, the task gradient remains material, or redundancy does not grow linearly with modulus.
reusable_insights: Separate geometric identity from functional equivalence: compare projectors, information alignment, causal effects, and operator invariants independently.
Require both core-only and core-removed interventions, but accompany them with manifold-preserving and random-subspace controls.
Fit operators only after holding out transitions, not merely examples, when claiming recovery of dynamical rules.
Checkpoint selection matters: a compact mechanism at task acquisition can become redundantly distributed under continued regularization.
For cross-model one-dimensional features, residualize ground-truth labels and prompt difficulty before treating coordinate correlation as mechanism alignment.
Quantify steering selectivity with target success, non-target behavioral preservation, language-model loss, fluency, and semantic drift rather than examples alone.
open_questions: Does ACE recover a unique core when challenged with the known non-identifiability and dormant-pathway counterexamples for subspace interventions?
How does ACE compare with PCA, PLS, DAS, sparse feature methods, and random-subspace search under matched rank and compute?
Can the grokking effect be tested by varying the number of redundant implementations while holding the task, vocabulary, dataset, and optimizer fixed?
Do independent models share an operator invariant after controlling for the common task labels rather than only coordinate correlations?
Can core-only interventions be constrained to the activation manifold or validated with causal mediation through the normal forward path?
Does a quantitative generation benchmark confirm broad, selective agreement control beyond is/are/was/were and templated noun attractors?
Are nonlinear or time-varying cores still compact for multi-step reasoning, induction, retrieval, or compositional language tasks?

competitive_landscape.title: Everything, Everywhere, All at Once: Is Mechanistic Interpretability Identifiable?
competitive_landscape.difference: This work exhaustively shows that multiple circuits, algorithms, and activation subspaces can satisfy behavioral and causal-alignment criteria. ACE is motivated by the same underdetermination problem but does not test its extracted cores against these non-unique explanations; it changes the explanatory target to equivalence-class invariants.

competitive_landscape.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
competitive_landscape.difference: Makelov et al. show that a behavior-changing subspace intervention can activate a dormant, causally disconnected pathway and therefore fail to localize the normal mechanism. ACE adds complementary necessity and sufficiency ablations, but does not supply the additional pathway-level evidence this antecedent argues is needed.

competitive_landscape.title: Universal Neurons in GPT2 Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Universal Neurons compares every neuron pair across five GPT-2 seeds over 100 million tokens and finds 1-5% recurring neurons with functional roles. ACE instead expects implementations to be geometrically different and seeks low-dimensional causal subspaces or operator invariants, extending beyond neuron identity but using much narrower LLM task data.

competitive_landscape.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
competitive_landscape.difference: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis studies increasingly aligned relational geometry across models, modalities, and scale and explicitly discusses counterexamples. ACE narrows convergence to task-specific causal subspaces and fitted dynamics, but its scalar LLM alignment is less able to distinguish shared geometry from shared labels.

competitive_landscape.title: Using Degeneracy in the Loss Landscape for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper classifies activation and Jacobian degeneracies and introduces an Interaction Basis intended to be invariant to their reparameterizations. ACE likewise combines activations and Jacobians, but emphasizes causal rank ablations and operator recovery rather than explicitly quotienting degeneracies; the overlap makes a direct method baseline important.

competitive_landscape.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Nanda et al. fully reverse-engineer the Fourier algorithm and identify memorization, circuit-formation, and cleanup phases using weights, activations, and Fourier ablations. ACE automates discovery of cyclic operators and adds post-grokking core inflation plus a redundancy scaling hypothesis, but offers less circuit-level validation of the recovered modes.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a conceptual shift from realization-specific circuits to invariant algorithmic cores, introduces ACE as an automated extractor of compact necessary-and-sufficient subspaces, recovers task operators without prespecifying them, explains weight-decay-driven redundancy and inverse grokking time, and identifies a universal one-dimensional agreement core across six LLMs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its strongest distinctive evidence is the same ACE workflow across a stochastic process, training-time modular arithmetic, and pretrained LLMs; exact Markov-spectrum recovery; the unexpected post-grokking core-inflation branch; and large complementary ablation effects for the rank-one agreement axes.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Cross-seed universality, representation convergence, degeneracy-invariant bases, mechanistic non-identifiability, subspace-intervention illusions, and Fourier grokking analyses all predate the work. The defensible novelty is the activation-Jacobian interaction SVD coupled to core-only/core-removed validation and operator fitting across these three regimes, plus the empirical core-inflation observation and its stylized redundancy law. The broad claim of invariant or universal cores is not established: subspaces are orthogonal, modular modes differ and inflate, scalar LLM correlations can be label-driven, and the generation result lacks quantitative selectivity tests.

reviewer_notes: Read all 17 pages of the current cached arXiv v2 source, including the complete ACE derivation, exact Markov tables, modular-addition implementation and transition holdout, subject-verb dataset and adaptive steering procedure, and grokking ODE/sweeps. Confidence is high in table transcription and in the narrow causal-ablation results, moderate in the operator-recovery interpretation, and low-to-moderate in uniqueness, cross-architecture universality, and the causal redundancy explanation. The linked code was not executed and the experiments were not independently replicated.
